approach.method_basis: The Parent generates new molecules by graph mutation and crossover, retains accepted scores for breeding, and uses a count-fingerprint Gaussian process to set candidate means, eligibility and correlated random draws. A frozen tabular quantile model supplies the residual distribution for each proposed molecule. Its adapter retains all count columns in eight views: variable columns use their fitted native transforms, while training-constant columns are centered on the first training row. Each native quantile curve is centered by its own integrated mean and added to the GP mean before sequential sampled-maxima selection.
approach.novelty: Activate the Parent’s existing same-width zero-C query control: replace each training-constant query count with its training value before native inference. This removes its nonzero query influence while keeping every column, view and variable-column transform. The resulting native quantile curve, with its own mean subtracted, drives actual purchases and feedback. There are no completed same-Parent siblings in the brief. Unlike the earlier joint adapter or the parallel marginal-shape intervention, this tests the conditional endpoint contribution of one already exposed input consumer.

observed_bottleneck: The code Parent n-ada68e100737 exposes query variation in columns constant in its accepted training archive, but its adapter changes full-width view layout and nonzero constant-column values together; their adaptive endpoint contributions are unidentified. It completed all fifteen Search cells with mean 0.5622564516615843 and seed population SD 0.005481732549278124. Full generating-parent positive gain rose to 16.68612674725103, while late gain fell to 3.915646383849673; endpoint mean remains 0.04477386454954668 below the formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de. Its passive same-width zeroed_constant control changes 194 of 435 selected sets and 247 active-only paid identities, versus 427 sets and 1440 active-only identities for filtered inputs. These are measured input exposures, not separate adaptive outcomes. The source-level operation and the paid-choice path therefore support this frozen validation question. The earlier native-location adapter ranking refutation in n-929b144c9731 remains intact; n-e2506e11f536 supplies the implemented GP-location host, not a claim that every native residual is beneficial. Evidence: nodes/n-ada68e100737/analysis.json; its seed-0/summary.json and run.log, seed-1/summary.json and run.log, seed-2/summary.json and run.log; policy/scratch/r0065-01-improve-L01/parent-audit-index.json and its fifteen audit-seed-N-task.json files, each citing the exact archived trajectory and allocation log.

hypothesis: At each real current-session refit let V_j = any_t(X_tj != X_0j) and C = complement(V), exactly as the Parent VisibilityEnsemble. Keep its accepted training X/y, full2048 identity filter, all eight none/power Latin views and exact fitted V transforms. At the native query boundary copy float32 x to x0 and set x0[:,C] = X[0,C], leaving x0[:,V] equal to x[:,V]. CenteredConstantPipeline then presents zero query C, exactly matching the Parent’s existing zeroed_constant operation; raw GP inputs continue to use x. Infer the native raw-unit 999-knot curve Q0, keep the inherited crossing handling and constant tails, and integrate its own mean m0. The only active allocation change is S_i = mu_GP_i + Q0_i(Phi(z_i)) - m0_i in place of the corresponding full-C law. Preserve Q0 shape and amplitude, including exact constant laws; introduce no Gaussianization, rescaling, column dropping, V-only view construction, query fitting or extra random draws. Use this same zero-C boundary for allocation, purchased native prediction records and next-context native probes. Its causal path is removed nonzero C input -> changed native centered law -> changed actual paid choices under fixed same-state GP mask and latent draws -> changed accepted fitting/breeding history -> signed conditional endpoint contribution. Shape and scale changes caused by x0 are consequences of this single input intervention and receive no separate attribution. The directional working prediction is that this removal loses more than 0.002 in matched macro endpoint, supporting material positive retained nonzero-C contribution.

finding_summary.headline: Removing query-only C input lowers endpoints, supporting its conditional retained contribution
finding_summary.insights:
This resolves the exposed input-consumer question that a passive zero-C replay could not answer: keeping nonzero query-C information contributes positively to the adaptive endpoint on this matched panel even when full feature layout, views and GP-centered residual sampling stay in place. The result does not isolate particular coordinates, prove that the feature layout itself helps, or separate the shape and scale consequences of changing inputs. Training-defined preprocessing, the native ensemble/target-inversion interface and own-law moment integration all operated; their full-width input adaptation and constant-tail residual use remain campaign-specific deviations from the literature. The conditional contribution is therefore narrower than a claim about the published predictor or the whole approach.

The method still concentrates some productive chemistry into related families. The molecular assessment finds that one amine-rich stream contracts from fourteen to three leading generic frameworks, while another keeps the same scaffold counts but its leading-molecule similarity rises from 0.356 to 0.597. A different aromatic-carbonyl stream broadens, so uniform scaffold collapse would be an inaccurate diagnosis. Oversized products fall from 112 to 59, yet tiny fragments persist and small-ring cyclic allenes rise from 192 to 243. These changes do not establish the cause of endpoint loss, but they show why less size inflation and more nominal scaffold identities do not assure productive chemical alternatives. A proposal operator that supplies coherent core/linker or ring-topology alternatives could address this observed limitation; simply adjusting residual magnitude would not supply those structures. The improvement in late local gain alongside lower final endpoints also shows that a phase-specific parent-beating metric cannot replace endpoint evidence. Which search or ranking scheme turns local progress into a higher final best score remains open, and this node does not settle the approach’s future.
finding_summary.results: The intended input removal executed cleanly across all 15 task/seed cells. Every one of the 435 allocation pools contained query variation in training-constant coordinates: 59,944 of 69,600 candidate rows had such variation. The active model consumed zero at those coordinates while preserving the full-width eight-view layout, variable-coordinate transforms, GP location and shared latent draws. All 420 next-context predictions also followed the new boundary, although their newly accepted inputs had no remaining C exposure. Relative to the same-state full-C diagnostic, residual curves changed for 59,944 candidates, 182 selection sequences and 176 selected sets changed, and 237 actual purchases were unique to the zero-C selection. All 4,350 purchased scores and feedback histories joined successfully; 4,200 purchases entered their next fits and 150 terminal purchases were correctly censored. Mean endpoint fell from 0.562256 to 0.552427: the paired difference was -0.009829, with population dispersion 0.005368. All three seed-macro differences were negative, while seven of fifteen task cells improved and eight worsened. This satisfies the registered strict -0.002 criterion for positive contribution of retained nonzero C in this composition. Full generating-parent positive gain fell from 16.6861 to 13.5158, but late-half gain rose from 3.9156 to 4.5899. The formal Anchor target of 0.609030 remains unmet.

molecular.headline: Aromatic polycycles and amine-rich rings remain abundant; size inflation falls, but strained unsaturation and unspecified stereochemistry persist
molecular.overall_character: Node n-cfa00d1cee11 is described using the complete frozen Search panel, seeds 0/1/2, against code Parent n-ada68e100737. context.comparison separately marks child_complete=true and paired_complete=true; all 15 Child and all 15 published Parent trajectories were readable. No task or Parent comparison is missing. Each arm contains 4500 accepted observations, including 150 initial and 4350 optimizer rows; this is not a census of unevaluated pools or rejected proposals. The digest has 900 rows and 870 optimizer rows per task. The molecules mainly contain fused, bridged or linked aromatic rings, carbonyl-bearing nitrogen heterocycles, aryl amides/ketones, ethers, halogens and, in some streams, aliphatic amines and sulfur functions. Child optimizer heavy-atom counts span 1–120 with median 30, versus Parent 1–117 with median 29; median perceived ring/aromatic-ring counts are 4/3 in both. Digest ring-closure rates are 0.9851–1.0 and aromatic-text occurrence rates 0.9816–0.9989; these are proportions of molecules carrying the notation, not aromatic-atom fractions. All digest charge and stereocentre annotation rates are zero; neutral SMILES do not imply absent protonatable amines. Both size tails remain visible: <=6-heavy-atom products number 22 versus Parent 23, while >=60-heavy-atom products number 59 versus 112. Global unique nonempty typed/generic Murcko scaffolds are 1585/981 versus 1813/1122. These counts exclude the empty acyclic scaffold and must not be conflated with historical totals that include it. RDKit structural flags count N–halogen molecules 424 versus 719, O–halogen molecules 217 versus 269, and small-ring cyclic allenes 243 versus 192. Allene perception here requires the central carbon and its two double-bond neighbors to share a ring of at most seven atoms; historical counts using other definitions are not interchangeable. Unassigned stereocentres occur in 2056 versus 1836 products, with assigned centres in none. Ordinary functional groups coexist with unusual N/O-halogen bonds, strained fused rings, cyclic cumulenes, repeated-core growth and unspecified stereochemistry. Makeability and stability are qualitative concerns; no synthesis, conformational validation, pKa, ADME or activity measurement was performed. Fragment-excluded top30 similarity is a descriptive within-task comparison: pool optimizer rows across seeds, retain the thirty highest recorded scores, exclude molecules with <=6 heavy atoms, then average all 435 pairwise radius-2 2048-bit Morgan Tanimotos. No cross-task score ranking is used. Per-task high-score scaffold and similarity comparisons follow below; neither similarity nor these chemistry associations attributes an effect to the intervention. Exact provenance and reproducible descriptor definitions are in policy/scratch/r0065-01-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-audit.json and its audit.py. Per-cell audits are policy/scratch/r0065-01-improve-L01/audit-seed-<seed>-<task>.json for each of the frozen panel cells. Each cites its exact underlying input file and SHA256. Child originals are the request-authorized .worktrees/slot-1/runs/staging/seed-<seed>/trajectories/<task>.jsonl files, outside the run; labeled byte-identical audit copies are policy/scratch/r0065-01-improve-L01/molecular/inputs/child/seed-<seed>/<task>.jsonl. These copies are not published node archives and do not expand the frozen citation authority. Parent sources are the existing nodes/n-ada68e100737/seed-<seed>/trajectories/<task>.jsonl files. The audit manifest enumerates every actual path; no future archive path is claimed. This report makes no mechanism, endpoint-contribution, ranking or selection verdict.

per_task.generated_character: These are mostly compact aromatic carbonyl compounds: indole-like aryl amides, fused nitrogen-containing aryl ketones and partially unsaturated fused rings with methoxy/ethoxy, alkyl, thioalkyl or halo substituents. Optimizer heavy-atom counts span 3–43, median 24; the top30 span 23–26. The seed-0 best is a four-ring, three-aromatic-ring fused N-heterocycle joined through a ketone to chloropyridine. Seed 1 retains an aryl amide on an unsaturated fused ring with chloromethyl/imine substituents; seed 2 retains an indole amide with N–S and thioethyl substitution. Conventional amides, ketones and ethers look chemically accessible in isolation; the unusual fused closures and N–S motif weaken confidence in the complete graphs. The top30 contain 11 typed and 5 generic scaffolds versus Parent 4 and 1; pairwise similarity is 0.299749 versus 0.374959, so this stream is not simply more collapsed than Parent.
liabilities: Repeated-core enlargement and one tiny fragment lose the observed productive extent.
Several promising structures contain N–S, imine or strained fused-ring connections; high benchmark score does not establish their stability or synthetic route.
missing_features: Reliable retention of a compact connected aromatic/carbonyl arrangement is missing at the low-score extremes, although it is clearly available in the successful structures.

The trajectory does not identify a unique absent target pharmacophore. Broader conventional alternatives around the productive carbonyl-bearing cores remain a hypothesis, not a demonstrated score requirement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-0 best scores 0.4463521672202675; replacing its ring chlorine with fluorine gives the same recorded score. Seed-1 and seed-2 best scores are 0.42348216717712805 and 0.43643070309403553. Fluoroethane scores 5.317476627259414e-17, and a much larger repeated indole–amide assembly scores 4.781022105091588e-14. The visible contrast supports retention of a compact aromatic/carbonyl assembly rather than disconnected size reduction or repeated-core expansion; it does not identify one obligatory amide or halogen. Parent best scores by seed are 0.4387992465191, 0.4033121758994662 and 0.4619578459378901, with related carbonyl-rich aromatic motifs. The chemistry/score relation is local and mixed across seeds.

per_task.generated_character: This stream is dominated by large N-rich aromatic assemblies: fused azaarenes connected to carbonyl-rich N-methyl heterocycles, frequently with multiple related ring units and halo, imine or thioether substituents. Heavy-atom counts span 1–120, median 39, compared with Parent median 44. The seed-0 best has 37 heavy atoms and nine perceived aromatic rings; the seed-1 and seed-2 best have 48 and 35 heavy atoms. The large tail contains 31 products with >=60 heavy atoms versus Parent 73; both arms still emit six products with <=6 heavy atoms. Dense nitrogen/carbonyl substitution and overlapping fused rings make many whole structures synthetically questionable despite recognizable constituent groups. Top30 generic scaffold counts are 6 versus Parent 5 and similarity is 0.563933 versus 0.606220.
liabilities: Large repeated-core structures and dense fused-ring topology can require difficult or implausible assembly; fewer oversized products does not remove this concern.
N–halogen and O–halogen motifs remain in this stream, including N–F in a seed-leading molecule; these are structural alerts, not measured instability.
missing_features: Tiny low-score products lack the connected aromatic/heterocyclic context present in higher-scoring products.

The observed plateau does not reveal which absent decoration or core would improve it; ordinary linker/core alternatives beyond repeated related N-rich units remain insufficiently resolved by these trajectories.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The digest spans 0.5–0.6066480311132718 with median 0.58933. FCl, CF and an acyclic ether sit at the 0.5 floor, while several substantially different N-rich polycycles share the top value 0.6066480311132718. Thus assembled aromatic heterocyclic context differentiates these observed leaders from trivial fragments, while many peripheral or fused-ring changes are weakly discriminated. Child seed best values are 0.6066480311132718, 0.5980392156862745 and 0.5942490398221144; Parent values are 0.608359133126935, 0.5936416783072068 and 0.6324541616056452. Parent seed 2 obtains its stronger value with a large linked aryl/azaaryl carbonyl heterocycle rather than requiring the Child seed-0 topology. Smaller size alone cannot explain the endpoint pattern.

per_task.generated_character: Higher-scoring products combine hydrophobic aryl/fused-ring surfaces with neutral aliphatic amine centres that could be protonated; sulfur appears as thioether or thiol, and phenols and halogens also occur. The seed-2 best contains an exocyclic tertiary amine, sulfur-containing ring, fused carbocycle, aryl phenol and carbon-bound Br/F substituents. Seed 1 uses a secondary aminoalkyl side chain and a constrained N-containing fused/bridged core. Heavy-atom counts span 9–109, median 29; the top30 span 24–30. Lower-score starting descendants often retain sulfonyl/amide-rich polar groups with nitrogen attached to electron-withdrawing functions. Top30 generic scaffolds contract to 3 versus Parent 14 and similarity rises to 0.457241 versus 0.337264; many nominally unique products are close members of the same high-score families.
liabilities: Every top30 molecule in both arms has RDKit-detected unassigned stereochemistry; bridges, substituted rings and unsaturated linkages do not specify a single three-dimensional compound.
Thiol/thioether functions, benzylic halogen substitution and tightly fused rings require stability, conformation and synthetic-route checking; the trajectory provides none.
missing_features: Accessible aliphatic amine centres together with a connected hydrophobic ring framework are absent from several low-score examples, but are already well represented among the leaders; a global claim that the generator cannot make basic amines would be false.

Alternative conventional constrained amine frameworks are less represented in the Child top30 than in Parent. No specific missing pharmacophore beyond this observed local association can be established.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-2 best scores 0.9999894390790366 and seed 1 reaches 0.9959585613348232. The low examples score 0.00016650955053713697 for an N-chloroamide/pyrrolidine sulfonamide and 0.00024675866379847753 for a small aryl sulfonate ester. Within these trajectories, connected hydrophobic rings plus accessible aliphatic amines associate with stronger scores than these smaller or amide/sulfonyl-dominated products. The seed-0 best is 0.9719597540616259 versus Parent 0.9999974292469022; Parent seed-1/2 values are 0.9845482536896144/0.9937212305252073. This does not show that adding an amine alone causes improvement, nor does the near-ceiling benchmark score establish experimental receptor binding.

per_task.generated_character: The productive family joins propyl/ethoxy-substituted aromatic rings to fused indole-like or N-rich ring systems and expanded lactam/urea-containing rings with N-methyl aliphatic amines. Heavy-atom counts span 1–67, median 32; top30 products span 31–35. The best has 34 heavy atoms, four rings and three aromatic rings, with adjacent carbonyls and an enlarged nitrogen-containing ring. Seed 1 makes a more fused N–N-containing polycycle; seed 2 retains a carbonyl-rich heterocycle plus a substituted cyclic diamine. These are more elaborate than ordinary small amides and amines, and constructing their full fused/macrocyclic arrangements is questionable without a route. Top30 typed/generic scaffold counts are 20/13 in both Child and Parent, yet similarity rises from Parent 0.355957 to Child 0.597116, illustrating why scaffold counts alone do not capture chemical concentration.
liabilities: Expanded polyamine/lactam rings and congested fused connectivity can increase synthetic difficulty and conformational ambiguity.
Unassigned stereochemistry appears in 18 of the top30 products; eight optimizer products have >=60 heavy atoms while fifteen have <=6, so both overassembly and fragmentation remain.
missing_features: Tiny low-score fragments have lost the connected aromatic and polar-ring arrangement associated with stronger scores.

The high-score family lacks broad independent ring/linker alternatives at comparable chemical similarity, despite multiple formal scaffold identities. No unseen target structure or mandatory substituent can be inferred from the modest observed score range.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best molecule scores 0.24630203781352464, while related cyclic urea/lactam compounds reach 0.2399780092147862 and 0.23972723494127993. Methane and acetylene score zero. The fixed initial carbonyl-rich aromatic heterocycle scores 0.1678386594791329. Larger connected aryl/heteroatom arrangements and the later amine/lactam ring extensions associate with better scores than fragmentation in this sample; the data do not prove a particular ring expansion is independently responsible. Seed-best Child values are 0.24630203781352464, 0.23293022583408315 and 0.21231495965326483 versus Parent 0.2338424221286825, 0.23322566212666948 and 0.23666901586613867. Related but different Parent aromatic/lactam frameworks remain competitive.

per_task.generated_character: These products are fluorinated carbonyl-rich nitrogen heterocycles with partially saturated or unsaturated small rings, phenols/ethers and, in one branch, sulfur-containing rings. Heavy-atom counts span 12–54, median 28; top30 products span 26–28. The seed-1 best has a large N-rich carbonyl ring bearing a fluorocyclobutene and a substituted four-membered ring containing cumulated double bonds, plus N–F and fluoroalkyl/fluoromethyl ether groups. The seed-2 best is a fused carbonyl-containing N-heterocycle with a sulfur/nitrogen ring, fluoromethyl group, phenol and N–F. The seed-0 best also contains N–F, N–O and an acyl fluoride. These are graph-valid outputs with especially questionable chemical stability and makeability. The digest cumulated-double-bond text rate is 0.2782; RDKit flags small-ring cyclic allenes in 242 optimizer products versus Parent 180, and N–halogen in 311 versus 217. Top30 generic scaffolds are 10 versus 9; similarity is 0.321505 versus 0.342906.
liabilities: Cumulated double bonds inside very small rings are a strong strain concern; valid SMILES and a favorable scalar score do not establish an isolable molecule.

N–F/O–halogen bonds, N–O linkages and acyl fluoride substitution need chemical justification and synthetic evidence; ordinary carbon-bound fluorination cannot be treated as interchangeable with these environments.
missing_features: A dependable set of conventionally bonded, unstrained alternatives at the productive molecular extent is missing from much of the high-score family: 26 of the top30 have N–halogen, two have O–halogen and thirteen have small-ring cyclic allenes. These flags may overlap.

Explicit stereochemical identities are absent even though all top30 products have unassigned centres. Their score benefit is untested; no missing primary amine or named target scaffold can legitimately be deduced from these trajectories alone.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best is 0.5579560963905262; seed-2 best is 0.5229339566573906 and seed-0 best is 0.44086142538278583. A bulky multi-core amide/acid assembly scores 3.5331505272531085e-35 and another repeated heterocycle assembly scores 1.8616241793622707e-26. The visible gradient favors a narrower molecular extent and particular fluorinated/carbonyl heterocycle arrangements over those bulky combinations, while tolerating chemically concerning bonds and ring strain. Parent seed-best values are 0.49317199895702235, 0.6054215806683655 and 0.5147249403189217; its seed-1 leader uses carbon-bound fluorination on a small ring without N–F. Thus N–F is not shown to be a necessary route to high score. The scalar scores do not identify which property or substructure causes the difference.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-cfa00d1cee11 compared with n-ada68e100737, complete frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, all accepted optimizer rows. N–halogen/O–halogen counts fall to 424/217 from 719/269, but small-ring cyclic-allene counts rise to 243 from 192 under the explicit shared audit definition. One high-score family contains N–halogen in 26 of its top30 and small-ring cyclic allenes in thirteen; a published Parent leader in that same stream has carbon-bound fluorination without N–F. This shows available alternatives, not that an alert causes endpoint loss. Exact provenance is retained in policy/scratch/r0065-01-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-audit.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve conventional bond environments and low-strain alternatives around promising ring systems.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make chemically coherent local alternatives available that preserve useful connected cores while changing problematic heteroatom-halogen bonds or small-ring unsaturation. Use current-session feedback to test them; a structural alert is not permission to hard-code an objective answer or assume that blanket rejection improves scores.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-cfa00d1cee11 versus n-ada68e100737 under the complete frozen Search panel: <=6-heavy-atom products are 22 versus 23, and >=60-heavy-atom products are 59 versus 112, out of 4350 optimizer rows per arm. CCF, C, C#C and FCl occur in trusted Child trajectories at near-zero, zero or observed floor scores, while some repeated-core assemblies also score very poorly. Higher-scoring examples occupy different connected size ranges across streams; neither uniform shrinking nor growth follows from this evidence.
transferable_gaps.gap: Connectivity is still lost at the small-size tail and overassembled at the large-size tail.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support edits that retain useful ring/linker/functional-group assemblies while controlling accidental fragmentation and repeated-core expansion. Learn productive molecular extent from the current session, retaining both tails as diagnostics instead of installing a task-specific size target.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-cfa00d1cee11 paired with n-ada68e100737 on the frozen Search panel. Unique nonempty typed/generic scaffolds fall to 1585/981 from 1813/1122. In one amine-rich stream the top30 generic frameworks contract from fourteen to three, with fragment-excluded mean pairwise Morgan similarity increasing from 0.337264 to 0.457241. Another stream keeps twenty typed/thirteen generic top30 scaffolds in both arms while similarity increases from 0.355957 to 0.597116. An aromatic-carbonyl stream instead broadens from one to five generic top30 scaffolds. The limitation is conditional, not uniform collapse.
transferable_gaps.gap: Raw graph and scaffold diversity do not guarantee distinct productive core chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer coherent core/linker and ring-topology alternatives alongside peripheral substituent edits, and inspect productive-family similarity separately from unique SMILES or nominal scaffold counts. Retain alternatives through task-local evidence; these chemistry associations do not identify which algorithm component caused concentration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-cfa00d1cee11, complete Search seeds 0/1/2, compared with n-ada68e100737. Digest stereocentre annotation rates are zero throughout. RDKit detects unassigned centres in 2056 of 4350 optimizer products versus Parent 1836, with no assigned centres in either arm. Two high-score ring-rich families each have unassigned centres in all thirty leading products. This records missing representation, not measured stereochemical score sensitivity.
transferable_gaps.gap: Promising three-dimensional molecular graphs remain stereochemically unspecified.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support internally consistent stereochemical alternatives for substituted rings, bridges and other stereogenic environments when the representation and scoring interface distinguish them. First establish sensitivity within the permitted session; this evidence alone does not justify spending evaluations on arbitrary stereoisomer enumeration.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
